title: Kolo ŋwane kunkwanu tem na ye yiga yiga to

rows.english: Long ago
rows.kasem: Faŋa na kɛ to

rows.english: Long, long ago, the land and the sky were close together. Clouds hung low over the compounds, within reach of an outstretched hand.
rows.kasem: Faŋa faŋa to, tega baŋa de wɛ yuu deem twɛ daane mo. Kunkwanu deem bwola de konkwalo, ye nmo na zeiŋi n jega, n wo yi te.

rows.english: At dusk, children gathered around an elder to hear how everything had changed.
rows.kasem: Didaani ne, bia lage nɔnkwea tei se b ani ko na ke tei ye woŋo maama leiri to.

rows.english: Shall I tell you a story?
rows.kasem: A wane a ta sensɔla a bere abam na?

rows.english: Yes! We are listening!
rows.kasem: Aa! Dé cheiga!

rows.english: Clouds for the cooking pot
rows.kasem: Kura kambia kunkwanu tem

rows.english: People fetched clouds and cooked with them.
rows.kasem: nɔɔna yeini ba kwooni kunkwanu ye ba mae ba saŋe

rows.english: When it was time to cook, people lifted their calabashes and gathered pieces of cloud. A little went into each cooking pot.
rows.kasem: Ko na yi saŋem maŋa, nɔɔna zeiŋi ba na zwe ye ba la kunkwanu. Fenfee yeini mo ko zo kura kambia maama.

rows.english: A child reached for one more handful, but an elder smiled.
rows.kasem: Bu tei o jeŋa o mɔ jaguli yi, ye nɔn kweo nyeke.

rows.english: Gather only what we need for cooking.
rows.kasem: La kolo de na wo mae de saŋe to yerane.

rows.english: There is enough for everyone!
rows.kasem: Kowo yi nɔɔno maama!

rows.english: An old witch
rows.kasem: Kani-cherega

rows.english: Then an old witch began pounding fufu in her courtyard. Her pestle was unusually long.
rows.kasem: Kani-cherega nam maa bobo ka zɔ sakɔra ka konkwɔlɔ ne. o sibia kam tiini ka dɔrema dedɛ.

rows.english: Each time she lifted the pestle, it hit the low sky. She frowned at the clouds above her.
rows.kasem: Maŋa kalo maama o na zeiŋi o sibia kam, ko yeini ko mage wɛyuu kom mo. O nyɔne o yibia de kunkwanu tem na we o baŋa ne to.

rows.english: Thump, knock! Thump, knock!
rows.kasem: pɔ, bam! pɔ, bam!

rows.english: My fufu must be smooth!
rows.kasem: Amo sakɔra kam ye se ka ke mɛtɛɛ mo

rows.english: fufu
rows.kasem: sakɔra

rows.english: The first warning
rows.kasem: Kaanem yaga tu

rows.english: A voice came from above, calm but clear. God warned the old witch.
rows.kasem: Kwara nam maa nuŋi wɛ ne ka, ka jege zurim ye ka taa ye jase. wɛ kaane kani-cherega kam.

rows.english: Old woman, listen to me.
rows.kasem: Kania, cheigi amo taane.

rows.english: Stop hitting the sky.
rows.kasem: ye ta n zɔ wɛ yuu kom

rows.english: Lower your pestle. Each time you lift it so high, you strike the sky.
rows.kasem: Pase n sibia kam vo tega ne, nmo na yeini n zeiŋi ka konto, n mage wɛyuu kom mo.

rows.english: She paused, glanced upward, and tightened her grip.
rows.kasem: O cheigi zɔɔne dem, o ni wɛ ne, ye o ta dare o  fɔŋe o nam zeeri sibia kam lanyerane.

rows.english: Another warning
rows.kasem: Kaanem belei tu

rows.english: But the old witch would not listen. She began pounding again, and her pestle struck the sky once more.
rows.kasem: Kani-cherega kam nam baa cheigi taane. O daa bobo zɔɔne mo. O sibia kam daa ma mage wɛyuu kom.

rows.english: God warned her again. Her neighbors hurried into the courtyard and begged her to stop.
rows.kasem: wɛ daa maa kaane o. o daa tiina de maa ba o konkɔlɔ kom ye ba lwoori o se o yage.

rows.english: Please listen. We all cook with these clouds.
rows.kasem: Pwopwo cheigi. Debam maama mae kunkwanu tento mo de saŋa.

rows.english: Let the sky move. I am not finished!
rows.kasem: Pa wɛyuu kom fɔɔre, amo ta wo ti!

rows.english: She waved the neighbors away and raised her pestle again.
rows.kasem: O ti o daa tiina bam o yage dɛ ne ye o dare o daa zeiŋi o sibia kam.

rows.english: The final warning
rows.kasem: Kaanem delo na kweili to.

rows.english: For a third time, God warned her. Everyone in the courtyard fell quiet.
rows.kasem: betɔ baŋa ne, wɛ kaane o. nɔɔno maama konkɔlɔkom ne to pugi ba ni.

rows.english: If you keep striking the sky, I will raise it beyond your reach.
rows.kasem: Nmo na jege wɛyuu kom n maga, amo wo zeiŋi ko wɛwɛ se n daa ye yi ko.

rows.english: The old witch lifted her pestle higher than before.
rows.kasem: Kani- cherega kam nam maa zeiŋi o sibia kam o dwoni.

rows.english: Just one more blow!
rows.kasem: A zɔ bedwe yerane a woli da!

rows.english: Knock!
rows.kasem: Chu!

rows.english: Up and away
rows.kasem: Baŋa yiga yiga

rows.english: God made the sky rise.
rows.kasem: wɛ maa pa wɛ yuu kom vo baŋa baŋa

rows.english: Up past the roofs, up past the tallest trees, up beyond every reaching hand. The clouds went with it.
rows.kasem: Baŋa baŋa ko gaale sane yum, ko gaale teini delo na dɔrema de dwoi to, baŋa baŋa ko gaale mɛ nabiinu jeŋa na baa yi to. Kunkwanu tem maa tɔge wɛyuu kom te di.

rows.english: The clouds! They are going away!
rows.kasem: Kunkwanu tem! Te maa kea!

rows.english: The villagers reached upward, but the clouds slipped farther away.
rows.kasem: Nɔɔna bam maama zeiŋi ba jea, ye kunkwanu tem vere te kɛ yiga yiga.

rows.english: The old witch lowered her pestle at last, but the sky kept rising.
rows.kasem: Kani-cherega kam nam pɛ o sibia kam vo tega, ye wɛyuu kom ta vei baŋa baŋa.

rows.english: From that day onward
rows.kasem: Ko zege dɛ dem konto taa wuu

rows.english: That evening, the pots waited beside the hearth. Nobody could fetch a single cloud.
rows.kasem: Didaani dem konto, kambi sem maa jei da konto mo. nɔɔna ware ba kwooni kunkwanu

rows.english: Can we ever reach the clouds again?
rows.kasem: Dé wo fɔŋe de yi kunkwanu tem daka na?

rows.english: The elder looked at the distant sky before answering.
rows.kasem: nɔnkwea kam ni wɛyuu kom yiga yiga to ye o nam leiri.

rows.english: That is why we must listen when we are warned.
rows.kasem: Konto ŋwaane mo de ye se de cheigi ba na kaane debam to.

rows.english: And from that day, the sky and the clouds remained far above the land.
rows.kasem: Ko zege dɛ dem konto, wɛyuu kom de kunwanu tem maŋe baŋa baŋa mo, tega kam yuu ne.
